title: Admin Briefcase: Delegatable runbook scriptlet converter and safe-exec fabric
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an "admin briefcase" capability that automatically converts verified runbooks into small, delegatable 'scriptlets' (idempotent, typed steps) that first-line support or automated agents can execute with strict RBAC, audit trails, and reversible side-effects. The briefcase provides a safe-exec fabric: sandboxed dry-run, pre-checks, telemetry risk scoring, and automatic rollback tokens. This reduces time-to-restore for common incidents and enables safe delegation while preserving SLOs and compliance.

Motivation and scope: Support teams currently escalate many high-frequency ops tasks to engineers because existing runbooks are long, require elevated creds, or lack clear guardrails. We will: 1) design a converter that ingests canonical runbook YAML/markdown and emits typed scriptlets with runtime validation; 2) implement a runtime harness (briefcase) that enforces policy gates, issues ephemeral credentials, and logs signed provenance; 3) provide a dry-run/sim sandbox and smoke verification for every generated scriptlet.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: long-form runbook authoring UI, export to external ticketing systems, and integrations with third-party ITSM (will be follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Converter accepts existing runbook formats (markdown with metadata or YAML) and produces a scriptlet manifest with typed inputs and explicit side-effect declarations
Briefcase runtime can execute a scriptlet in dry-run mode and surface a deterministic plan and resource access list
Ephemeral credentials are issued via the credential broker for only required scopes and bound to a single execution token
All executions emit structured audit events compatible with the ops telemetry pipeline and are viewable in Console runbook traces
A safety policy engine blocks scriptlets with unchecked destructive actions and surfaces remediation steps
Merge candidate PR (#1827) with converter code and unit tests merged to repo 'ops/briefcase' and E2E pipeline producing a sample scriptlet manifest
comments: 2025-03-10 - Aisha Patel: initial ticket. Collected 18 canonical runbooks from 'ops/runbooks/canonical' for sample corpus. Attached sample markdowns. Marking P1 because this unlocks support autonomy.

2025-03-12 - Liam O'Connor: spike complete. PoC converter parses 12/18 runbooks into typed steps; identified 3 common anti-patterns: undocumented side effects, implicit credential usage, and global state mutations. PoC branch: github.com/redwood/ops-briefcase/pulls/178

2025-03-13 - Noor Martinez (oncall): validated PoC against a non-prod incident (db failover drill). Dry-run plan matched expected actions and flagged an unscoped 'ssh' step—converted to 'bastion-proxy' step in manifest
2025-03-14 - Security review (initial): request to add KMS envelope for rollback tokens and HSM-backed signing for provenance events. Assigned to Security team for follow-up (SEC-312).
2025-03-16 - Product review (Evan Chu): requested UX hooks for Console to present 'briefcase consent' to support agents and a compact audit view. Filed PM follow-up PM-5591 for Console surface.

2025-03-18 - Liam O'Connor: integrated credential broker flow and added smoke E2E; tests passing in CI. PR opened: github.com/redwood/ops-briefcase/pulls/1827. ETA for merge: 2025-03-20 pending security sign-off and 1 more integration test.
decision_log: 2025-03-11: Chose typed-scriptlet manifest over opaque command blobs to enable static analysis and policy checks
2025-03-12: Decided to bind ephemeral creds to execution tokens (least privilege) rather than embedding static secrets in manifests
2025-03-13: Opted for KMS-enveloped rollback tokens and signed provenance events instead of plaintext undo scripts
2025-03-14: Selected policy engine 'Sentinel-lite' for initial gating with future migration path to full policy marketplace
implementation_notes: Converter architecture: parser -> canonical AST -> step normalizer -> manifest emitter. Keep normalizer rules configurable so we can add company-specific transforms (eg: replace 'ssh' with 'bastion-proxy').
Runtime harness: containerized executor with network egress filters, syscall sandboxing for dangerous ops, and explicit resource allowlists pulled from manifest
Telemetry: emit start/plan/commit/rollback events with signed metadata (runbook id, scriptlet version, executor id, token hash) to 'ops/exec-events' topic
Safety: add a pre-exec 'plan diff' that computes expected resource deltas; if risk score > threshold, require 2nd-op consent or engineer approval
Testing: build synthetic incident simulator to validate idempotency and rollback across 3 common failure modes (partial failure, timeouts, and credential expiry)
next_steps: Complete security review (SEC-312) and incorporate HSM signing hooks
Merge PR #1827 after adding one integration test for credential expiry scenario
Wire Console consent flow (PM-5591) and add 'briefcase' tab to runbook traces
Run a staged pilot with oncall rotation for two weeks using 6 converted scriptlets
Document governance: lifecycle for scriptlet updates, authorship, and scheduled re-validation
blockers: Security sign-off for rollback token KMS envelope (SEC-312)
